answer: Timed Arrival Shaping. Each identity must pass a quartz-gated clock: its first N actions are admitted only inside randomized arrival windows drawn from a slow reference schedule. A bridge process matches the arrival timing distribution against that schedule before forwarding to the vault. Clones arriving in bursts miss their windows and stall until re-queued. The cost is calendar time per identity — an attacker launching 10,000 Sybils must spread registrations across thousands of separate windows, paying hours of serialized latency rather than one batch fee.
